findings.summary: Acceptance control schemas remain mutable after the frozen revision, and the reviewed validator prohibits only three hard-coded capability field names. Starting from a schema-valid synthetic READY/ACCEPT descendant bound to frozen commit 0aa4a7a72ff672004d1be9e38e781ab09b395929, I changed acceptance_decision.schema.json to require a new runtime_storage_write_authorized property with const true and added runtime_storage_write_authorized=true to acceptance_decision.json while retaining runtime_migration_authorized=false, airtable_historical_write_authorized=false and public_capability_change=false. Canonical --require-ready returned success. A post-frozen schema can therefore introduce a new capability authorization outside the reviewed digest. The completed-review path must byte-bind the acceptance decision schema, preferably every review control schema, to the frozen commit or the reviewed validator must enforce an exact closed decision-key set independently of mutable schemas.

The round-3 review-request replacement attack is closed. The completed-review path compares current review_request.json bytes with the frozen commit. Removing CONTENT_GOVERNANCE.md from review_scope, replacing both pre-issued reviewer identities, recomputing the digest and artifacts, and adding post-frozen authorization text now fails canonical --require-ready with review request identity/scope does not match the frozen commit.

The exact round-3 capability attack is closed for the three declared fields. Changing their schema constraints to true and setting runtime_migration_authorized, airtable_historical_write_authorized and public_capability_change to true fails through direct checks in reviewed validator code, independent of the mutated schema wording.

Prior artifact-integrity and identity controls remain effective: open finding counters are recomputed, fabricated reviewer identities fail pre-issued-slot matching, unsafe paths remain rejected, artifacts are digest-bound, distinct tracks and instances are required, and a nonexistent frozen Git commit fails before READY.

The independently replayed review-scope digest exactly equals 1f7ca23d70da78127636a5c506684cc99cd65e7b432ae742402922f70161d02d. Frozen Git commit/tree identity and ancestry are exact, lifecycle normalization remains restricted to approved status/version transitions, canonical --require-ready rejects custom package/schema inputs, and the synthetic legitimate READY transition succeeds before adversarial mutation.

Complete semantic collection locks, closed collection identifiers, duplicate-key rejection, source artifact and locator integrity, globally unique IDs, bidirectional Claim/EvidenceLink/Uncertainty closure, non-local uncertainty rejection, append-only replay and current-frontier determinism remain fail-closed under the focused suite and controlled mutations.

ACCEPT requires READY with two READY reviews, while DECIDED NARROW and REJECT outcomes must bind the registry frozen commit and tree. Pending decisions cannot claim frozen identity or a decision, and canonical READY remains tied to one exact frozen commit, tree and reviewed digest.

Remote PR #378 points to the supplied commit, whose Git tree is exactly 981d09662d90e7b56a152237cd5c7c4c7a644714. The fixture validator passes, 50 focused tests pass, Release Check passes, git diff --check passes, and the immutable #329/#330 fixture directories, frozen Gate C package and project_state.json are unchanged. At observation time the dedicated Progressive Refinement workflow and eight other workflows were successful; the remaining general ETL Check was still in progress.

The temporal and spatial refinement remediations preserve immutable #330 semantics: temporal refinements retain the calendar/normalization profile and every primary or alternative member must be contained in the predecessor possible set; spatial-only refinements cannot mutate inclusivity, qualifiers, calendar, normalization state or alternatives.

conclusion: The supplied remote commit, tree and reviewed digest are exact, the focused and release checks pass, and both specific round-3 control-plane attacks are closed. However, the mutable post-frozen acceptance schema can introduce a new capability-authorization field not covered by the validator's three-name prohibition, and canonical --require-ready accepts it. The round-4 candidate is therefore CHANGES_REQUIRED.
